resolution: D-435 rewritten: NaruServe hands close 1001 to every session's sender slot, waits min(1 s, time left to the D-162 deadline), then aborts via UpgradedConnection.close() (verified: Upgraded.close -> Connection.abortSocket) every session whose close task has not returned, regardless of earlier write age. The bound rests on the abort alone: WebSocket takes conn.getOutputStream() once so output wrapping is possible, but not needed, since TinyHttpd's ping/pong/close all write under the same writeLock and a socket close makes the blocked write throw (open=false/closeSent), making TinyHttpd's later fireStop close(1001) return at once. D-344 counts that wait inside the deadline; new D-439 adds the stalled-client T44 test.
Same fix as V2-001: no 1 s age threshold; every session whose close has not completed within the bounded wait is aborted, which also covers TinyHttpd read-thread Ping/Pong writes.
D-425: the scheduler only detects idle sessions, hands close 1001 to the session's D-417 sender slot and schedules a 1 s check that aborts the socket; it never writes or waits on a session.

New D-436: SSE closing is a before-wait participant that enqueues a closing notice (exempt from the queue limit) and marks the stream ended without waiting, so the drain loop ends and onClose runs before the adapter stop waits. D-401 names WebSocket and SSE closing as before-wait participants.

New D-440: when applying D-431, wave 5 rewrites kotlin.md examples that assign req.body(...) to a non-null type or dereference it, makes the shown extension body compile, and sets the nullability row to T?.
New D-437 documents TinyHttpd's per-line header cap of inputBufferBytes - 2 (RequestParser.parseHeaders lineMax = buf.length - 2, answered 431) in defaults.md, separate from the maxHeaderBytes total.

D-426 now passes through FAILED to TERMINATED (D-159, object.md 11.3). New D-438: a shutdown timeout during STARTING returns normally, state STARTING or FAILED, pending stop kept. D-427 waits only up to its timeout, consistent with D-438.
